Camera

Switch cameras any time before starting.

Live viewfinder resolution

Downsizing only affects the live viewfinder to keep preview smooth and lag-free. Captured photos and prints always save at full maximum camera resolution.

Camera photo resolution

Shot timing

Auto checks how far the live picture is behind the real scene and lines the photo up with "Pose". If photos are still blurred because guests have already moved when the camera takes the picture, choose a time to take the photo earlier: try 0.4 s, then raise it until photos are sharp.


          
          
          
On: guests see themselves like in a mirror. Saved and printed photos
            match the preview.

          

            
            
Keeps the camera sensor, light and mirror idle when not in use to save power and prevent heating.
              On: the camera runs only during a guest's session and on this Camera step, and stays idle on the welcome screen (wakes in about a second
              when a guest taps Start). The preview here pauses after 2 minutes without a touch; touch the screen to resume. Off: always on.

            
            
A Sony can't switch its live view off over USB, so after 10 minutes with no guest the booth lets go of it and the camera can rest.
              It reconnects when someone touches the screen (about 3–5 seconds). If your Sony switches itself off after that, turn this off or raise its Power Save time.

            

          

          

            

              🎯 Focus Setup & Test Shot
              dslrBooth style
            

            

              1. Set lens switch to AF (Auto Focus).

              2. Have someone stand in position, then tap Auto-Focus Lens or Take Test Shot.

              3. Once sharp, switch lens switch to MF (Manual Focus) so every event shot fires instantly with zero delay!
            

            

              
              
            

            

              

                Test Shot Result
                
              

              
              

            

            

              🔋 Camera Battery & Heat Tips (Nikon D5300 & DSLRs)
              
    
                
  • Lens VR switch: OFF — Turn off Vibration Reduction on the lens. VR stabilization gyros run constantly during Live View on a tripod and drain ~30% more battery.
    • 
                
  • Lens Focus switch: MF — Once focused using the button above, set the lens to MF so focus motors never hunt or draw power.
    • 
                
  • Fold Screen Inward — Flip the D5300's swivel screen facing the camera body to completely shut off the rear LCD panel and backlight.
    • 
                
  • In Camera Menu: Turn Image review to OFF, and turn Wi-Fi and Location data (GPS) to OFF.
    • 
                
  • Custom Setting c2: Set Auto off timers to Short (6s standby) so the exposure meter sleeps immediately between sessions.
    • 
                
  • Mode Dial: M (Manual) — Set shutter to 1/125s, f/8, ISO 200/400 (with flash/strobe) so the camera doesn't compute auto-exposure continuously.
    •

                  Prints gibberish, strange text or gaps?
                  
Small mobile printers (58mm) can lose data if it arrives too fast. Run the checks in order and stop at the first one that goes wrong.

                  

                    
                    
                    
                  

                  
Text fine but the picture garbles? Pick Slow and safe (58 mm paper only) and Compatibility below, then check again. If the picture already prints right, keep Automatic and Standard: the slower settings can leave faint lines across it. Nothing prints at all? Power the printer off and on (do not hold FEED), then try 1 again.

                  

                    
                    
                  

                

                
Thermal print too
                  dark? Increase Lightness / Exposure (+20 to +40) in Print settings above to lighten the output.
